pages.text: The yard's zelkova tree had thick, strong branches. An old nail stuck out of the wall. Yuki dragged out a thick rope.
"I'll hang a swing here." Yuki dropped the rope in the grass. Momo plopped down beneath the tree.
A flat piece of wood lay behind the house. Yuki leaned it against the wall and turned away. "I'll fetch it later."
Grandma gave Yuki a bundle of short cords. Yuki pushed them under the porch. "They can stay here."
Yuki stood beneath the zelkova with empty hands. "Now I just need to hang it."
Yuki peered under the porch. Only the cords were there. "Where did I put the rope?"
Thick summer grass made everything green. Even searching through it did not reveal the rope. "I can't hang it today."
Grandma went to the wall and tapped the old nail with her palm.
The next day, Yuki found the rope in the grass. "I can hang it there."
A swing swayed from the zelkova. Short cords hung on the wall's nail. Momo circled beneath the swing.
